papers.title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations
papers.abstract: Poisson equations frequently appear in various fields, such as mathematics, physics and informatics. Solving Poisson equation, however, is challenging. Traditional methods are not data-specific, although have high certainty. They require a large number of iterations due to the CFL numerical stability. In contrast, deep learning methods are data-driven and more efficient, but require accurate training data and suffer from heavy computation. To tackle these issues, we propose a wavelet-inspired Poisson solver with 24 trainable scalars. The proposed network has several advantages. First, it is compact. It has four independent $5\times5$ kernels, each represented by six parameters, leading to 24 scalars in total. Such compact format can be deployed on most devices. Second, thanks to the loop design, it achieves higher accuracy than previous methods. A residual loop reuses the wavelet block without increasing its parameters. Numerical experiments confirm that such loop indeed improves the solving accuracy. On 10000 images, one, two, and three loops of the wavelet block lead to PSNRs of $47.27$, $74.14$, and $100.74$ dB, respectively. Third, the proposed method is computationally fast. Thanks to the wavelet transform, the proposed method has linear computation complexity, leading to high computation performance. In short, we propose a novel looped wavelet neural network with compactness, accuracy and efficiency for solving Poisson equations. Our method can be applied in various fields, such as computational fluid dynamics, image reconstruction, biomedical engineering, electromagnetic field simulation.

papers.title: Convergence of alternating score-system iterations for regularized Landau particle dynamics
papers.abstract: We analyze an alternating iteration for score-based particle approximations of the homogeneous Landau equation. Each step computes a regularized score along the previous trajectory and recomputes the trajectory with that score frozen. First, at fixed positive regularization, we prove existence, uniqueness, and $W_1$-Lipschitz stability of a Tikhonov score minimizer in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space embedded in $C_b^2$. For bounded Lipschitz collision matrices, this yields factorial convergence to the coupled regularized dynamics on every finite interval, with constants independent of particle number. Global objective gaps and system residuals control inexact solves, and structural kernel assumptions ensure momentum and energy conservation. The mean-field and alternating-iteration limits commute at fixed regularization in this regime. Second, score-difference cancellation extends the theory to far-field-truncated Landau kernels with $\gamma \geq -2$ and the uncut case $\gamma=-2$. For the uncut three-dimensional Coulomb kernel, a separate continuum construction gives local factorial convergence from bounded, compactly supported densities. Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.

papers.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
papers.abstract: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.

papers.title: Logarithmic Stability for the Inverse Boundary Problem in Three-Dimensional Isotropic Elasticity
papers.abstract: We establish logarithmic stability for the simultaneous recovery of both Lam\'e parameters in three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity from the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The $L^\infty(\Omega)$ estimate holds uniformly on every fixed bounded $C^{22}$ class of uniformly strongly convex coefficients, without prescribed exterior coefficients, agreement of boundary values or derivatives, or smallness assumptions on material gradients. For every integer $s\ge2$, we also obtain boundary stability estimates with exponents $(s-q)/s$ for all Cartesian derivatives of orders $0\le q<s$, where the measurement error $\delta$ is the operator-norm discrepancy between the Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps. These exponents are sharp on admissible classes containing a constant material satisfying the a priori inequalities strictly. On such classes, no uniform modulus of continuity exists for boundary derivatives of order $s$. The proof combines an exact four-component reduction with finite-regularity complex geometrical optics constructions, while deriving complete matrix-valued integral identities from the Betti identity for elastic displacements. An amplitude annihilated by the leading physical adjoint lift produces, at the first nonvanishing order, the third polarization in a rank-three characteristic quotient. Holomorphically weighted matrix moments, Cauchy--Plemelj factorization, and a fixed holomorphic projection then yield quantitative control of the relative transport and recovery of both coefficients. Boundary stability estimates and paired extensions transfer the analysis from an auxiliary common-exterior setting to the original measurement domain. The exact-data argument also establishes global uniqueness for $C^{22}$ Lam\'e parameters.

papers.title: On Convergence to Equilibrium for the Boltzmann Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We study relaxation of correlated solutions of the hard-cutoff Boltzmann hierarchy toward factorized Maxwellian equilibrium. We prescribe the Maxwellian's mass, momentum, and energy in each full particle coordinate, conditional on the others. Centering removes these conserved modes, but collisions still couple each centered level to the next. To control this forcing uniformly in particle number, we combine adapted second-order Sobolev tensor norms with geometric activity weights and prove $\frac12\frac{d}{dt}E_z(H(t))^2 +(\lambda-\sqrt{2}C_\Gamma z)D_z(H(t))^2\le0,$ where $H$ is the rescaled centered hierarchy, $E_z,D_z$ measure its energy and dissipation, and the coercivity and collision constants $\lambda,C_\Gamma$ are independent of particle number. For small activity $z$, dissipation absorbs the coupling and gives contraction and uniqueness in the hierarchy energy. Time-dependent weights yield level-proportional exponential decay. For global solutions, densities and observable generating functions converge to equilibrium, and connected pair correlations decay at twice the one-particle rate. The estimates apply to existing energy solutions. General existence remains an assumption, while statistical mixtures, including continuous laws, of sufficiently regular one-particle solutions uniformly close to the reference Maxwellian, with common conserved moments, provide examples.

papers.title: Homogenization of degenerate parabolic Signorini problems with vanishing storage and oscillating surface fluxes
papers.abstract: We study the homogenization of a unilateral quasilinear parabolic problem in a periodically perforated medium. The model combines two degeneracies: the coefficient of the time derivative is non-negative and may vanish, while the directional diffusion weights are positive almost everywhere but need not be bounded away from zero. The exterior boundary carries a Signorini condition, and the holes carry an unscaled zero-mean flux oscillating on the diffusive time scale. For any family of microscopic solutions we prove strong space--time $L^2$ compactness through a weighted detection inequality, which replaces the Aubin--Lions lemma when the storage vanishes, and we recover spatial $H^1$ regularity of the limit by a closed-range argument for the weighted two-scale gradients. The limit solves a coupled two-scale problem in Minty form, and microscopic existence holds under joint monotonicity. Under a strengthened condition, the limit decouples into a macroscopic Signorini inequality whose uniqueness follows from an exponential regularization, without time regularity of the limit, and the whole family converges. The surface datum enters both the effective flux and the exterior boundary condition.

papers.title: Axisymmetric Navier--Stokes with Swirl: Regularity and Blow-Up Constraints
papers.abstract: For smooth finite-energy axisymmetric Navier--Stokes solutions with swirl, we give a continuation criterion in terms of the signed cumulative work of the actual post-cut source-generated meridional current, with quartic viscous dissipation counted once. In the stated strong Sobolev class the criterion is necessary and sufficient and requires neither a global circulation bound nor spatial moments. We also prove cumulative inward-compression criteria, collect quantitative necessary conditions at a first singular time, and give a complete-history mixed-residual test for noncontinuation. Auxiliary results quantify quartic dissipation, energy-funded source bounds, and causal source--receiver identities. An explicit smooth whole-space datum has positive newborn source production.

papers.title: $L^p$-regularity for fourth-order Schr\"odinger operators with unbounded or degenerate coefficients
papers.abstract: We prove that operators of the form $A=-\Delta^{2}-V(x)$, with $|D V(x)|\leq \gamma V(x)^\frac{5}{4}+ C_\gamma$ for some $\gamma$ small enough and $C_\gamma$ positive constant, generate analytic semigroups in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for $1\leq p<\infty$ and in $C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Moreover, we characterize the maximal domain of such operators.

papers.title: Variational mean curvatures for general $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ domains
papers.abstract: The notion of variational mean curvature (VMC) arises from Massari's variational approach to hypersurfaces of prescribed mean curvature and expresses a minimizing property for Massari's functional. Here, we complement the theory of VMCs with a new sharp relation between hypersurface regularity and VMC integrability. In fact, our main result asserts that every bounded open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ boundary, $0<\alpha<1$, has a global VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for every $p<\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}$. In addition, we underpin sharpness of this conclusion by constructing examples of bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ boundary which do not admit a VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for any $p>\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}$. Our proofs are based on Barozzi's level-set construction of global VMCs and determine integrability of these VMCs by geometric investigation of their superlevel sets and of related unions of balls.

papers.title: Nonradial Finite-Time Blow-up for the Mass-Critical Inhomogeneous Biharmonic NLS
papers.abstract: We consider the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous biharmonic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ i\partial_tu=\Delta^2u-|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{8-2b}{N}}u, \quad 0<b<\min\{4,N/2\}. \] We prove that every $H^2(\mathbb R^N)$ solution with negative energy blows up in finite time, both forward and backward. No radial symmetry or finite-variance assumption is required. In particular, this rules out the global grow-up scenario in the previously known negative-energy blow-up alternative and establishes finite-time blow-up in the genuinely nonradial setting. The proof relies on a new localized virial argument exploiting the spatial inhomogeneity to control the localization errors.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and orbital stability of the Gross--Pitaevskii branch in a coupled defocusing Schr\"odinger system
papers.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional coupled defocusing Schr\"odinger system with a nonzero background in its first component and finite mass in its second component. We prove global well-posedness in the full energy space, together with conservation of energy, bright mass, and total untwisted momentum. For all nonnegative coupling coefficients, every subsonic Gross--Pitaevskii soliton with vanishing second component is orbitally stable against perturbations of both components, including the zero-speed black soliton. At nonzero speed the proof uses a fixed energy--momentum functional augmented by the conserved bright mass. At zero speed it uses weighted coercivity and a local real lift of the momentum. We also identify the sharp threshold for positivity of the unaugmented bright energy and explain why this threshold is not a necessary condition for orbital stability.

papers.title: On the annular overdetermined problems with linear and power nonlinearities in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study two classes of partially overdetermined elliptic problems on planar annular domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with a fixed inner circle and a free outer boundary. The Dirichlet values are prescribed to be $1$ and $0$ on the inner and outer boundaries, respectively, while the squared normal derivative is constant on the outer boundary. For the linear law $\Delta u=-\mu u$, we establish local bifurcation under a Dirichlet nonresonance condition. For the power law $\Delta u=u-u^p$ with $p>1$, we take the mean outer radius as the bifurcation parameter and construct large positive radial solutions on thin annuli. The limiting profile solves $-V''=V^p$ on an interval, and the principal mixed Dirichlet--Neumann eigenvalue of its linearization determines a constant $\kappa_p>0$. For every fixed inner radius $\lambda>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $K$, we obtain a critical radius $R_K=\lambda+\lambda\kappa_p/K+o(K^{-1})$ and a smooth local curve of positive solutions with noncircular, even, $2\pi/K$-periodic outer boundaries. The proof combines shape derivatives, spectral estimates, and the Crandall--Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem.

papers.title: A frequency localized maximum principle and its applications to time fractional equations with rough coefficients
papers.abstract: We establish a frequency localized maximum principle for parabolic second-order partial differential equations with the Caputo time fractional derivative $\partial_t^\alpha$ of order $\alpha\in(0,1)$. The leading coefficients are uniformly elliptic, measurable in time, and independent of space. We construct suitable equivalent norms on frequency localized subspaces of $L_\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, for which a frequency localized maximum principle holds. The corresponding result may fail in the usual $L_\infty$ norm even for the classical heat equation. As an application, we prove existence, uniqueness, and regularity estimates in Sobolev-Zygmund spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in time for equations with spatially variable coefficients and zero initial data. The coefficients are strongly measurable in time with values in a H\"older-Zygmund space of positive order and uniformly bounded in this space.

papers.title: The Neumann problem for stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Neumann problem for second-order stochastic partial differential equations in the half space. The coefficients are random and merely measurable in time. We develop a class of weighted function spaces for this problem, and establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity results. In contrast to the Dirichlet problem, the Neumann problem admits solutions with improved boundary regularity under suitable assumptions on the coefficients and data.

papers.title: Curvature Effects on Boundary Accumulation of Self-Propelled Particles: A Fokker-Planck Approach
papers.abstract: It is well known that self-propelled particles tend to accumulate near boundaries. Although the influence of boundary geometry on this accumulation has been extensively studied using individual-based models, a population-level PDE description becomes desirable when a large number of particles are involved. In this work, we investigate boundary accumulation of self-propelled particles confined in two-dimensional circular and annular domains. We develop Fokker--Planck models that qualitatively reproduce the behavior observed in individual-based simulations. The main contribution is the formulation of appropriate evolution equations for particles accumulated at the boundary, incorporating transitions between the interior free-swimming state and the boundary-contact state. Starting from a general spatial two-dimensional model, we simplify the associated boundary conditions by assuming radial symmetry and then design an exponentially weighted difference scheme that preserves the total mass of the coupled system. Because transitions between different particle states induce singular behavior near the boundary, establishing discrete mass conservation is nontrivial. In particular, the velocity space must be divided into two subdomains, with the resulting discontinuity treated explicitly. Stochastic simulations and numerical experiments are performed both to validate the proposed models and to investigate the effects of geometric and dynamical parameters on boundary accumulation.

papers.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
papers.abstract: We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-\lambda u \quad \text{in }\Omega. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $\lambda>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $\lambda$ and constant for sufficiently small $\lambda$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $\lambda\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

papers.title: The fractional Calder\'on problem on finite Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: We study a Calder\'on-type inverse problem for the spectral fractional Laplacian on finite Cayley graphs. For a known self-adjoint operator, recovery from a single measurement reduces to two requirements: full rank of the boundary (exterior)-to-interior coupling and nonvanishing of the interior solution. We verify both requirements on Cartesian products of arbitrary finite groups with even cycles, using consecutive cyclic halves as the accessible and inaccessible sets. Fractionalization increases the coupling rank, and one fixed nonnegative nonzero input determines every nonnegative potential. Our argument relies on a discrete maximum principle and an explicit resolvent formula.

papers.title: Sharp Wasserstein stability and small-delay thresholds for evolution equations with measure-valued principal-part delays
papers.abstract: We study the dependence of solutions to coercive evolution equations on the law of a measure-valued delay acting through the principal spatial operator. For non-negative delay measures of equal mass, transport couplings and the time-translation modulus of one reference trajectory yield quantitative kernel-stability estimates. Fractional temporal regularity gives a Wasserstein rate, with explicit glueing and data criteria for its application. For moving point delays in a diffusion model, a solution-level lower bound matches both the rate and its dependence on the kernel mass. This matching estimate holds for zero prescribed history and uniformly bounded forcing in the natural dual energy space. The results also quantify concentration to positive delays and approximation by atomic quadrature. Separately, we determine a sharp class-level threshold for energy bounds uniform in the delay location. At the critical threshold, any fixed scalar mode is spectrally stable, but uniform space--time energy control fails in a small-delay, high-frequency limit. Above the threshold, the growth has an explicit asymptotic logarithmic rate.

papers.title: Symmetry and Monotonicity for Subcritical Fractional Hartree Equations with Singular Sets of Zero Capacity
papers.abstract: We study positive weak singular solutions of the subcritical fractional Hartree equation \[ (-\Delta)^s u = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma} \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}d y \right)u^q \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(N>2s\), \(0<\mu<N\), and \(\Gamma\subset\{x_1=0\}\) is compact with zero \((s,2)\)-capacity. For solutions with a nonremovable singular point on $\Gamma$, we prove hyperplane symmetry and strict transverse monotonicity under global Lebesgue integrability conditions. For $N\ge2$, we also prove these conclusions under upper bounds on $p$ and $q$, using only the integrability required for weak solutions. We also establish local regularity and construct solutions with logarithmic singularities along a line segment.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions II
papers.abstract: This is the second of two papers on isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation on manifolds with nonflat background metrics. In the first paper, we proved that, in dimensions $3\le n\le29$, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a radial model singular solution in the flat metric on the Euclidean space with origin as its singular point---a Fowler solution. In the present paper, we show that this dimension range is sharp. More precisely, for each $n\ge30$, we construct a smooth metric on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ and a positive solution of the corresponding Yamabe equation having an isolated singularity, near which the solution blows up along a sequence at a rate much faster than that of Fowler solutions. Moreover, the singular solution defines a complete conformal metric of constant positive scalar curvature and the metric agrees with the round metric to infinite order at the singular point.

papers.title: Universal H\"older estimates for stable solutions to semilinear equations of fractional order
papers.abstract: We establish universal interior H\"older and fractional energy estimates for stable solutions of $(-\Delta)^su=f(u)$, $0<s<1$, with $f\in C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R})$ nonnegative and convex. The bounds depend only on a weighted $L^1$ norm of the solution and hold under optimal conditions on the dimension and the fractional order. In particular, the half-Laplacian estimate holds through dimension eight. The estimates extend to stable finite-energy Dirichlet $L^1$-weak solutions without an a priori local boundedness assumption, and an explicit logarithmic solution proves optimality in this class. Applications include global bounds in convex domains, bounded extremal solutions, and a Liouville theorem.

papers.title: Interior gradient estimates for mean curvature equations on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study interior gradient estimates for solutions of \[ \operatorname{div}_{M}\left(  rac{
abla u}{\sqrt{1+|
abla u|_g^2}} ight) =f(x,
abla u) \] on a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. Under a Ricci curvature lower bound and a Hessian comparison for the distance function, we derive polynomial and exponential gradient bounds under structural conditions on $f$ and its horizontal and vertical derivatives. The estimates explicitly separate the contributions of curvature, distance comparison, and the dependence of $f$ on the base point and the tangent vector. As applications, we obtain Liouville-type results for entire solutions under suitable curvature and growth assumptions.

papers.title: Sharp Capacity Estimates and Volume Growth for Fractional Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp two-sided estimates for the relative capacity of fat and thin annuli in the fractional Sobolev spaces $W^s_{p,q}$, where $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,\infty)$, $q\in(0,\infty]$, in terms of an explicit volume growth quantity. The underlying space is a general metric measure space equipped with a doubling and reverse doubling measure. In particular, whenever the capacity is finite, the estimates are independent of the parameter $q$. For $p<q$, we also introduce a sharp condition on the underlying measure that is necessary for the existence of admissible functions in $W^s_{p,q}$ space.

papers.title: Generalized Logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on Bounded Domains and exponential decay to Boltzmann states for Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes systems
papers.abstract: We derive logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on bounded domains for nonnegative functions that are prescribed on a portion of the boundary, and for Boltzmann-weighted reference measures. We use them to address the long-time dynamics of the Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes system with Dirichlet, blocking and mixed boundary conditions for the ionic concentrations and a Dirichlet--Neumann boundary condition for the electric potential. We prove that solutions converge exponentially fast to the Boltzmann steady states. When at least one species of each sign of valence is in contact with a reservoir, the asymptotic rate of convergence is independent of the dielectric constant and depends only on the domain, the boundary data, the masses of the blocked species, the valences, the diffusion coefficients, and the fluid viscosity.

papers.title: On the long wave limit of the good Boussinesq equation
papers.abstract: We consider the good Boussinesq equation on the line. Sufficiently regular solutions are known to converge in the long wave limit to a pair of counterpropagating solutions to the Korteweg--de Vries equation. We prove that this convergence holds for solutions in $H^{-\frac12}$, the largest Sobolev space in which the good Boussinesq equation is well-posed. As part of our analysis, we revisit the well-posedness theory, proving new a priori estimates and a corresponding small data global well-posedness result.

papers.title: Invariant and Super-median Functions for Perturbed Heat Kernels
papers.abstract: We study super-median and invariant functions for positive and negative Schr\"odinger perturbations of non-negative kernels. For positive perturbations, combining Dynkin's formula for the original kernel with Duhamel's formula for the perturbation, we derive perturbed Dynkin-type identities and give integrability conditions ensuring invariance. When the perturbed kernel is given by the perturbation series, we obtain a sufficient condition for a function to be super-median without additional integrability assumptions. We also decompose every finite non-negative solution of Duhamel's equation into the perturbation series and a non-negative solution of the corresponding homogeneous equation. For negative perturbations, we obtain analogous identities under an explicit finiteness condition. We also construct functions satisfying Dynkin's formula using zero-resolvents and compensated kernels. Examples involving Gaussian, fractional, and Bessel kernels illustrate the invariance criteria and the role of non-uniqueness in Duhamel's equation.

papers.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.

papers.title: Sharp Weighted Sobolev Trace Inequalities on Convex Cones and Rigidity of Extremals
authors: Lucas de Melo Pontes e Silva
papers.abstract: We study critical weighted Sobolev trace inequalities on convex cones endowed with positively homogeneous weights. Using mass transportation, we first establish the continuity of the critical trace embedding under general homogeneity and concavity assumptions on the weight. We then identify a compatibility condition between the weight, the cone, and a distinguished direction that makes the transport argument sharp. In this regime, we determine the optimal constant and prove the existence of extremals. Finally, we obtain a complete classification of all nontrivial extremals modulo translation in the lineality space.

papers.title: Local well-posedness of the two-dimensional Incompressible Schr\"odinger flow
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible Schr\"odinger flow (ISF), an efficient model for simulating incompressible inviscid fluids introduced by Chern et al. \cite{C17,CKPSW16}, on a bounded, simply connected two-dimensional domain. After transforming it into the director formulation, the equation becomes the Schr\"odinger map (or the Landau--Lifshitz equation) transported by a velocity field generated from the director itself via Biot--Savart law. We show that the director formulation has a unique local-in-time strong solution. Then, we lift the solution to the director formulation to the spinor, and conclude that it is indeed a unique solution to the ISF. This result is a first rigorous analysis on ISF, a widely used computational model.

papers.title: A Jost--Pais theorem for the intermediate long wave equation
papers.abstract: For a one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operator, the transmission coefficient can be expressed as a Fredholm determinant. This fundamental discovery of Jost and Pais has recently proven very influential in the study of conserved quantities for the Korteweg--de Vries equation, whose Lax operator takes this form. In this paper, we obtain an analogue of this result for the intermediate long wave equation, where, startlingly, the transmission coefficient is given by a \emph{ratio} of Fredholm determinants. We then recover the original Jost--Pais result in the shallow-water limit and its analogue for the Benjamin--Ono equation as the infinite-depth limit.
